implementation_notes: Scala's tour states the mechanism plainly: higher-order functions take other functions as parameters because functions are first-class values, and methods passed as arguments are coerced into functions. The owner is a method or component function taking State => Html (ScalaTags), State => VdomNode (scalajs-react) or a child Modifier parameter (Laminar), and the caller's function literal decides the markup; the classic structure disappears into the parameter. Curried parameter lists keep the state and the renderer visually distinct - def widget(state: State)(render: State => Html) - which is the idiomatic shape when the state is primary and the renderer is supplied second.
pitfalls: By-name versus function parameter: a => T argument is re-evaluated on every use inside the owner while () => T runs when invoked, so mixing the two changes how often the renderer runs and whether it sees fresh state.
Implicit/given parameters can smuggle state into the renderer without the caller seeing it, defeating the explicit-argument property that makes the pattern readable.
Function values allocate on the JVM unless the compiler can inline them; in hot rendering paths prefer one composed function over chains of small lambdas.
